$comment: Generated by tools/generate-conformance-fixtures.ps1 from a real PowerShell. Do not hand-edit: a hand-edited fixture is a claim with no engine behind it.

line-endings.why: The capture host is Windows and emits CRLF; the compatibility profile targets Linux and the runtime is a browser. A fixture that encodes CRLF could never match either.

machine-paths.why: Absolute paths differ on every machine. Replaced longest-first with <REPO>/<CWD>/<PSHOME>/<TEMP>/<HOME> so the most specific token wins.

username.why: The account name appears in paths, in provider output and in some error messages.

hostname.why: The machine name appears in remoting, provider and process output.

process-id.why: A pid changes on every run. Bounded by word boundaries so an unrelated number that happens to share the digits is left alone.

guid.why: A GUID is new on every run. New-Guid is in the corpus specifically so that omitting this rule would break the determinism check rather than pass silently.

iso-timestamp.why: Round-trip timestamps ("o" format) appear in DateTime output and in the capture metadata of nested objects.

clock-time.why: A bare wall-clock time survives the timestamp rule when a date is formatted separately from its time.

trailing-space.why: Table rendering pads columns to the pinned width. The padding is presentational -- no semantic depends on it -- and keeping it would make every fixture diff unreadable.

detectors.ansi-escape: Rendering is pinned to PlainText. An escape sequence means the pinning stopped working, which must be fixed rather than scrubbed.
detectors.carriage-return: The line-ending rule should have removed every CR. One surviving means it came from inside a string literal, where rewriting it would change the data.
detectors.windows-drive: A drive letter means the case is Windows-specific. The compatibility profile this project publishes targets PowerShell on LINUX, so such a case cannot be compared and must say so.
detectors.username-residue: The account name survived canonicalisation, so the fixture would only reproduce for this user.
detectors.bare-year: A four-digit year that no timestamp rule matched is almost always the wall clock leaking in through an unexpected format.
